title: Everyday Worship
description: Little Muslim → Mid. Short questions for children who know the first worship basics. Covers wudu, certainty and doubt, careful water use, iqamah, following the imam, calm prayer movements, forgotten prayers, praying according to ability, mosque practices, suhur, forgetful eating, fasting manners, Eid, dua, respectful charity and ability for Hajj. Includes familiar home and classroom situations. An adult may read questions aloud or explain unfamiliar words. All questions are Mid level within the Kids audience.
levelMethod: Mid describes the knowledge and understanding needed across all question styles. Styles are not difficulty levels. Builds on familiar names and routines with simple meanings, common misconceptions and straightforward everyday applications. No detailed legal disputes, specialist measurements, advanced travel rules or memorization of reference numbers is required. Level is editorial guidance, not calibrated with children's reading or response data. Quiz performance describes learning needs, not a child's faith or worth.

review.referenceCheck: Linked Quran passages and reports from Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim checked during preparation. Questions and explanations are original child-friendly educational paraphrases, not verbatim translations. Present-day situations illustrate applications; they are not events narrated in the cited reports. This is an introductory question bank, not a complete prayer, wudu, fasting or Hajj manual. A child's learning is not equated with an adult's legal responsibilities. Fasting scenarios involving legal outcomes explicitly use adults; no scenario directs a child to fast despite illness or beyond appropriate ability. Known passing of wind is distinguished from mere doubt. Sound and smell are not presented as the only possible evidence of broken wudu, and children are not encouraged to check their bodies repeatedly. Careful water use is an application of the reported modest water measure, not a fixed volume imposed on every learner. No disputed wording count is required for iqamah. Mosque-entry prayer questions avoid cases where the obligatory congregation has begun and do not settle differences about restricted times. A knowledgeable teacher should guide actual practice. Prayer according to physical ability is taught without judging disability or prescribing medical treatment. Forgotten prayer is distinguished from planning to neglect prayer. The report on forgetful eating is not permission to continue eating deliberately after remembering. Fasting conduct is taught without telling a child that a particular person's fast is legally invalid because of a lie. The two Eid days are identified without suggesting they are the only days with fasting restrictions. Dua questions do not promise that every particular request must be granted immediately or exactly as asked. Charity examples preserve dignity, allow suitable adult guidance and do not imply that all public giving is wrong. Hajj questions address the condition of ability, not its complete conditions or a child's duty to travel. This is not independent scholarly approval or a completed review with children.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: In wudu, washing the hands and arms extends up to which joints?

options.text: The elbows
The shoulders
The knees
Only the fingertips

questions.explanation: The Quran mentions washing the hands and arms up to the elbows. Learn the full steps with a trusted teacher.

questions.question: What happens to wudu when a person passes wind?

options.text: It becomes stronger
It is broken and needs renewing before salah
It changes the prayer direction
It lasts until the next day regardless

questions.explanation: Passing wind breaks wudu. Renewing wudu prepares a person to pray again; ordinary bodily functions are not a reason for shame.

questions.question: What does the hadith teach about merely doubting whether we passed wind?

options.text: Repeat wudu after every passing thought
Assume every worry proves wudu is broken
Do not treat doubt alone as certainty
Check repeatedly until learning feels impossible

questions.explanation: The hadith teaches not abandoning prayer because of imagined wind. A passing doubt does not undo known wudu.

questions.question: What does the report about the Prophet's ﷺ small amount of wudu water illustrate?

options.text: Wudu needs a whole swimming pool
More spilled water always means better worship
Washing properly is unnecessary
Wudu can be performed with modest water use

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ performed wudu using a modest measure of water. Careful use should still allow proper washing.

questions.question: Which call signals that the congregational prayer is about to begin?

options.text: Iqamah
Iftar
Suhur
Tawaf

questions.explanation: The iqamah is connected with starting the congregational prayer. It is different from the earlier adhan announcing prayer time.

questions.question: When praying behind an imam, how should we perform the prayer movements?

options.text: Race to finish before the imam
Follow the imam without going ahead
Choose an unrelated sequence
Ignore the imam's movements entirely

questions.explanation: The imam leads the prayer and is to be followed. Prayer together is not a race to move first.

questions.question: How did the Prophet ﷺ teach the man to bow and prostrate?

options.text: As quickly as possible
Without pausing anywhere
With calmness, settling into each position
While turning it into a competition

questions.explanation: The report teaches calm bowing, standing, sitting and prostration. Each movement deserves care rather than a hurried rush.

questions.question: What should a person do on remembering a prayer they genuinely forgot?

options.text: Leave it forever
Replace it with a game
Wait until the same date next year
Pray it when they remember

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ taught praying a forgotten prayer when it is remembered. Forgetfulness has a remedy rather than a reason to give up.

questions.question: If someone cannot stand for prayer, what alternative does the hadith teach?

options.text: Praying while sitting
Stopping every prayer forever
Forcing someone else to carry them upright
Mocking people who sit

questions.explanation: The hadith allows sitting when standing is not possible, and lying on one's side if sitting is not possible either.

questions.question: In the hadith about entering a mosque, how many rakahs are taught before sitting?

options.text: Five
Two
Seven
Ten

questions.explanation: The report teaches two rakahs before sitting in the mosque. A teacher can explain when and how to practice this.

questions.question: What does the reported dua for entering the mosque ask Allah to open?

options.text: A secret way to become famous
A path to hurting others
The doors of His mercy
Every locked cupboard

questions.explanation: The mosque entry dua asks Allah for His mercy. Learning its meaning helps connect familiar words with sincere worship.

questions.question: Why did the Prophet ﷺ encourage suhur?

options.text: It lets fasting begin at midday
It makes fasting on Eid necessary
It replaces every daily prayer
There is blessing in it

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ described blessing in suhur. This gives the meal before dawn a place in preparing for fasting.

questions.question: What should a fasting person do after eating or drinking completely forgetfully?

options.text: Stop on remembering and complete the fast
Assume the whole fast is lost
Keep eating deliberately until sunset
Stop fasting for the whole month

questions.explanation: The hadith tells someone who ate or drank forgetfully to complete the fast. Deliberate eating after remembering is a different matter.

questions.question: Which behavior does the hadith especially warn fasting people to leave?

options.text: Truthful answers
False speech and wrongdoing
Helpful actions
Respectful conversation

questions.explanation: Fasting includes care for our behavior. The hadith strongly warns against false speech and wrongdoing, not just eating and drinking.

questions.question: Which pair of days did the Prophet ﷺ forbid people to fast?

options.text: Every Monday and Thursday
Every Saturday and Sunday
Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha
The first two days of Ramadan

questions.explanation: The report forbids fasting on the two Eid days. Following worship guidance includes knowing when not to fast.

questions.question: In the Quran's teaching about dua, how does Allah describe Himself?

options.text: Unable to hear quiet requests
Interested only in famous people
Unaware that anyone calls upon Him
Near and responding to the caller

questions.explanation: Allah tells His servants that He is near and responds when they call upon Him. This encourages sincere dua.

questions.question: The dua beginning Rabbana atina asks for good in which two places?

options.text: This world and the Hereafter
Only the classroom and playground
Only two neighboring towns
Only today's meal and tomorrow's meal

questions.explanation: This Quranic dua asks for good in this life and the Hereafter, as well as protection from the Fire.

questions.question: What does the Quran warn against after giving charity?

options.text: Respecting the person helped
Hurtful reminders of our generosity
Speaking kindly to the person
Protecting the person's dignity

questions.explanation: Giving does not permit humiliating someone. The Quran warns against spoiling charity with reminders and hurtful treatment.

questions.question: What does the Quran say about giving charity privately to people in need?

options.text: It has no value without a crowd
It is always forbidden
It is better for the giver
It must be announced on a stage

questions.explanation: The verse praises charity and especially giving privately to the poor. Helping someone does not require an audience.

questions.question: Which condition does the Quran mention in the obligation of Hajj?

options.text: Owning the newest phone
Being the tallest family member
Winning a school competition
Being able to make the journey

questions.explanation: The Quran connects the obligation of Hajj with ability to reach the House. This is not a demand for every child to travel.

questions.question: Is washing only the fingertips the same as washing the hands and arms up to the elbows?

options.text: No, the washing includes more than fingertips
Yes, fingertips replace the whole washing
Yes, elbows are unrelated to wudu
No, because arms must never touch water

questions.explanation: Wudu has taught washing and wiping steps. Washing the hands and arms up to the elbows is not merely wetting fingertips.

questions.question: Does knowing that we passed wind differ from only wondering whether we did?

options.text: No, known wind never affects wudu
Yes, known wind means wudu needs renewing
Yes, known wind changes the adhan
No, every bodily feeling requires a new prayer timetable

questions.explanation: The teaching concerns an actual event that breaks wudu. Knowing it happened is different from having an uncertain thought.

questions.question: Does every uncertain thought mean that a person must repeat wudu?

options.text: Yes, repeat it after every worry
Yes, the more checking the better without limit
No, doubt alone does not undo known wudu
No, because actual wind never breaks wudu

questions.explanation: Known wudu is not treated as lost just because of doubt. Ask a trusted adult if repeated worries make learning difficult.

questions.question: Does using water carefully mean leaving the required areas unwashed?

options.text: Yes, skip washing to save effort
Yes, touching the tap replaces washing
No, because spilling more water always improves wudu
No, use enough to wash properly without needless excess

questions.explanation: Careful water use and proper washing go together. The report does not make a large amount of wasted water the goal.

questions.question: Are the adhan and iqamah simply names for the meal that ends a fast?

options.text: No, they are calls connected with prayer
Yes, both mean the evening meal
Yes, both mean eating before dawn
No, both are names for charity boxes

questions.explanation: The adhan announces prayer time; the iqamah signals the prayer's start. Neither is the name of a meal.

questions.question: Does praying in congregation mean trying to bow before the imam?

options.text: Yes, moving first earns a race prize
No, the imam is to be followed
Yes, everyone should ignore the leader
No, because nobody may ever bow

questions.explanation: The hadith teaches following the imam. Moving ahead of the leader misses that lesson of praying together.

questions.question: Is moving quickly through bowing and sujud the same as settling calmly in them?

options.text: Yes, speed is the only thing that matters
Yes, skipping stillness is always better
No, calm positions need proper attention
No, because prayer contains no movements

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ taught settling in the prayer's positions. Speed is not a replacement for learning them properly.

questions.question: Does the teaching about a genuinely forgotten prayer tell us to plan to miss prayers?

options.text: Yes, it encourages forgetting on purpose
Yes, it makes prayer time irrelevant
No, it says forgotten prayers can never be prayed
No, it explains what to do after forgetting

questions.explanation: The report gives a remedy for forgetfulness. It is not an instruction to deliberately ignore prayer times.

questions.question: Does needing to sit for prayer make someone less deserving of respect?

options.text: No, the hadith recognizes different physical abilities
Yes, only standing people deserve kindness
Yes, sitting always proves laziness
No, because all healthy people must lie down

questions.explanation: Prayer guidance takes inability into account. We should not mock a person for using a taught accommodation.

questions.question: Is the two-rakah prayer on entering a mosque a replacement for all five daily prayers?

options.text: Yes, it replaces the whole day's worship
No, it does not replace the daily prayers
Yes, one mosque visit replaces every future prayer
No, because praying in a mosque is forbidden

questions.explanation: The report teaches a prayer connected with entering the mosque. It does not cancel the five daily prayers.

questions.question: Does the mosque entry dua ask the building itself to grant mercy?

options.text: Yes, the walls answer the dua
Yes, the carpet decides who receives mercy
No, the request is directed to Allah
No, it asks people to worship the doorway

questions.explanation: The dua is addressed to Allah. Entering a mosque is an occasion to remember Him and ask for His mercy.

questions.question: Does the blessing of suhur mean the most expensive meal is always the best?

options.text: Yes, only costly food can have blessing
Yes, ordinary family food never counts
No, suhur is a contest to eat the most
No, the hadith does not set a price requirement

questions.explanation: The teaching praises suhur without making expensive food its condition. Families need not turn the meal into a spending competition.

questions.question: Are eating completely forgetfully and choosing to keep eating after remembering the same situation?

options.text: No, the report specifically addresses forgetfulness
Yes, both mean forgetting throughout
Yes, remembering never changes anything
No, because forgetful eating always ends every fast

questions.explanation: The hadith reassures the person who forgot. It does not permit deliberately continuing to eat after remembering the fast.

questions.question: Does avoiding food give a fasting person permission to tell lies?

options.text: Yes, hunger makes every lie acceptable
No, truthful behavior still matters
Yes, only food matters during fasting
No, because speaking truthfully ends the fast

questions.explanation: The hadith links fasting with leaving false speech and wrongdoing. Hunger does not become an excuse for dishonesty.

questions.question: Is fasting on Eid al-Fitr an extra improvement on following the Prophet's ﷺ guidance?

options.text: Yes, it is always the best Eid activity
Yes, eating on Eid is always wrong
No, fasting on that day is forbidden
No, because every Ramadan fast is forbidden

questions.explanation: Worship follows taught limits. The prohibition of fasting on Eid shows that more fasting is not always the correct choice.

questions.question: Does being ordinary or unknown to other people prevent us from calling upon Allah?

options.text: Yes, only celebrities may make dua
Yes, a large audience is required
No, but only competition winners may ask
No, His invitation is not limited to famous people

questions.explanation: Allah's teaching invites His servants to call upon Him. Fame and attention from other people are not requirements for dua.

questions.question: Does Rabbana atina teach us to care only about this worldly life?

options.text: No, it includes good in the Hereafter too
Yes, it excludes the Hereafter
Yes, it asks only for expensive belongings
No, it forbids every request for worldly good

questions.explanation: The dua includes both this life and the Hereafter. It teaches a broader hope than seeking only immediate possessions.

questions.question: Does giving someone charity give us a right to keep embarrassing them about it?

options.text: Yes, giving buys the right to insult
No, charity should not be followed by hurtful reminders
Yes, the person must accept every humiliation
No, because kind words make charity useless

questions.explanation: The verse warns against reminders and harm after charity. Helping someone should preserve their dignity rather than become control over them.

questions.question: Must every charitable gift be public for it to have value?

options.text: Yes, only gifts with applause count
Yes, a photograph is always required
No, private giving to the poor is praised
No, because all public charity is forbidden

questions.explanation: The verse recognizes public charity as good and private giving to the poor as better. It does not require publicity.

questions.question: Does the Quran's teaching about Hajj ignore whether someone can make the journey?

options.text: Yes, ability is never considered
Yes, everyone must travel immediately regardless of circumstances
No, because Hajj is only a school activity
No, ability is part of the teaching

questions.explanation: The verse mentions ability to reach the House. We should not use the topic to shame people about travel or money.

questions.question: A wudu lesson shows washing from the hands to the elbows. Which body area is being taught?

options.text: The hands and arms
Only the top of the head
Only the toes
The shoulders and back

questions.explanation: Match the washing area to the taught step. A parent or teacher can help you learn it correctly.

questions.question: Before prayer practice, Yusuf knows he passed wind after making wudu. What should he learn to do?

options.text: Pretend it never happened
Renew his wudu before praying
Change the qiblah instead
Repeat only the adhan

questions.explanation: Known passing of wind breaks wudu. Yusuf can calmly renew it, asking for help with the steps if needed.

questions.question: Amina remembers making wudu and has only an uncertain thought about wind. Which lesson applies?

options.text: Every thought proves she must restart
She must keep checking without stopping
A passing doubt alone does not mean wudu is broken
She should abandon learning prayer entirely

questions.explanation: The hadith addresses imagined wind. Amina need not treat a mere doubt as proof that her wudu has ended.

questions.question: During supervised wudu practice, which approach uses water thoughtfully?

options.text: Leave the tap running for fun
Skip washing the arms entirely
Spill as much water as possible
Wash properly using a manageable flow

questions.explanation: The reported modest water use encourages care. Ask the teacher to help you wash properly while avoiding unnecessary waste.

questions.question: Your teacher says the iqamah is being called. What is about to begin?

options.text: The congregational prayer
The meal before dawn
The end of Ramadan fasting
A lesson in planting seeds

questions.explanation: The iqamah signals the congregational prayer's start. Recognizing it helps you understand the order of familiar prayer routines.

questions.question: During prayer practice behind an imam, you want to reach sujud first. What should you remember?

options.text: Finishing first wins the prayer
Follow the imam rather than race ahead
Everyone must move in a different order
The imam's movement is unrelated to yours

questions.explanation: The imam is appointed to be followed. Learn the movements with care instead of trying to beat someone to the next position.

questions.question: In a prayer lesson, Hasan rushes through bowing without settling. What should his teacher help him practice?

options.text: Moving even faster
Skipping bowing altogether
Bowing calmly and settling into position
Turning prayer into a timed race

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ taught calmness in prayer positions. Patient instruction can help Hasan learn rather than embarrass him.

questions.question: An adult remembers a prayer they genuinely forgot. Which action follows the hadith?

options.text: Wait for a yearly reminder
Treat it as impossible to remedy
Replace it with buying a gift
Pray it when remembered

questions.explanation: The report teaches praying the forgotten prayer when it comes to mind. Children can learn this without judging anyone's faith.

questions.question: A relative cannot stand for salah. Which response reflects the hadith's guidance?

options.text: Respect their need to pray sitting
Call them lazy for being unwell
Demand that they stand despite inability
Tell them prayer has no accommodations

questions.explanation: The hadith teaches praying according to ability. Respect the person's situation; a knowledgeable adult can guide the details.

questions.question: At a suitable time, your teacher demonstrates the prayer taught before sitting in a mosque. How many rakahs are demonstrated?

options.text: Six
Two
Eight
Twelve

questions.explanation: The report mentions two rakahs before sitting. Follow a trusted teacher's guidance about its suitable practice.

questions.question: You enter the mosque with a parent and learn its entry dua. What meaning should you remember?

options.text: Asking the floor to answer prayers
Demanding that everyone praise you
Asking Allah to open the doors of His mercy
Asking for help to bully someone

questions.explanation: The entry dua asks Allah for mercy. Learning the meaning helps make the routine thoughtful rather than only repeating sounds.

questions.question: Your family prepares a simple suhur. Which reminder fits the Prophet's ﷺ teaching?

options.text: Only luxury food can count as suhur
The biggest meal always proves stronger faith
Suhur must become a family spending contest
There is blessing in suhur without a costly feast

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ encouraged suhur for its blessing. A simple family meal need not become a display of wealth.

questions.question: An adult drinks water while completely forgetting the fast, then remembers. What follows the hadith?

options.text: Stop drinking and continue the fast
Keep drinking on purpose
Declare every Ramadan fast ruined
Give up fasting for the year

questions.explanation: The report tells the forgetful eater or drinker to complete the fast. Remembering is the point to stop the forgetful eating or drinking.

questions.question: A lesson says fasting is only about an empty stomach. What important teaching should you add?

options.text: Hunger gives permission to deceive
Avoiding false speech and wrongdoing matters too
Every spoken truth ends a fast
Bad conduct becomes good during Ramadan

questions.explanation: The hadith warns against false speech and wrongdoing while fasting. Learning fasting includes attention to character as well as food and drink.

questions.question: A friend suggests fasting on Eid al-Fitr to earn extra credit. Which lesson should you share?

options.text: Eid fasting is always required
Eating on Eid cancels Ramadan
The Prophet ﷺ forbade fasting on that day
Every celebration must be spent fasting

questions.explanation: Not fasting on Eid follows the taught limit. You can explain it kindly and ask a teacher for help if needed.

questions.question: Lina thinks Allah's invitation to make dua is only for famous people. Which reminder fits the Quran?

options.text: A crowd must approve every dua
Only people with trophies may ask
Ordinary families are excluded from dua
Allah is near and responds to those calling upon Him

questions.explanation: The verse reassures Allah's servants about calling upon Him. Lina does not need fame or a public audience to make dua.

questions.question: Your teacher explains Rabbana atina. Which summary should you choose?

options.text: Ask for good here, good hereafter and protection from the Fire
Ask only for the most toys
Ask to forget the Hereafter
Ask for help to harm classmates

questions.explanation: This Quranic dua brings together good in both lives and protection from the Fire. Its meaning reaches beyond immediate wants.

questions.question: After helping someone, a child keeps saying, "You owe me praise." Which lesson should a teacher explain?

options.text: Giving earns permission for every insult
Give without using the gift to embarrass or control
The recipient must accept public shame
Kindness after giving has no importance

questions.explanation: The Quran warns against hurtful reminders after charity. Help should be offered with respect for the person receiving it.

questions.question: With a parent's permission, Sara gives quietly to a family in need. Must she post a photo for it to matter?

options.text: Yes, a photo is what makes it charity
Yes, only a large audience makes giving worthwhile
No, private charity to those in need is praised
No, because helping quietly is forbidden

questions.explanation: The Quran praises private giving to the poor. Sara can help with her parent's guidance without seeking public attention.

questions.question: A class discusses why ability matters when learning about Hajj. Which answer fits the Quran?

options.text: Every child must travel this week
Only famous families may visit
Travel costs and ability can never matter
The obligation mentions being able to make the journey

questions.explanation: The Quran includes ability in its teaching about Hajj. The lesson is not a competition about whose family can afford travel.
